name: Cyclone Arnab

moving.text: Arnab has weakened to a low over Chhattisgarh. The storm is over; recovery is under way.
moving.eta: No more cyclone threat from Arnab. New, separate system: IMD (Oct 31, 5:30 am) says a well-marked low in the southeast Bay should become a depression within 12 hours and reach near the Andhra coast by the evening of Nov 2. Isolated very heavy rain in coastal AP & Yanam on Nov 2–3. No cyclone forecast so far. Odisha: floods now only in Ganjam.

headline: Arnab is over, but more rain is coming. Andhra is in recovery: power is back in 92% of affected villages (APEPDCL) and the Howrah–Chennai line is running again. IMD says a new low-pressure system from the Andaman Sea may become a depression and head for the Andhra coast, with heavy to very heavy rain on Nov 2–3. Rivers are still high in Ganjam and Balasore (Odisha).

briefing.t: Arnab is over: it weakened into a low over Chhattisgarh (IMD, Oct 29). No cyclone alerts remain.
More rain coming: a new depression is likely to move towards the Andhra coast. Heavy to very heavy rain in coastal AP on Nov 2–3 (IMD). Fishermen stay ashore off AP Nov 1–4.
Power: 5,277 of 5,727 affected villages back (APEPDCL, Oct 30). Fully restored in Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram Manyam, Anakapalli, East Godavari, Kakinada, Eluru.

Konaseema is slowest: about 8,000 poles fell there (CM). AP's target is full power restoration by this evening, Oct 31 (Energy Minister). Mobile network: 384 of 1,045 towers were still down on Oct 30.
Howrah–Chennai main line fully open again since Oct 30, 3:45 pm (Ichchapuram–Jhadupudi bridge). Trains run at reduced speed.
Mobile network: 99.18% back in Andhra (DoT, Oct 31). Odisha: Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal improving.
Leaving a relief camp? AP gives 25 kg rice, an essentials packet and cash for immediate needs.
AP: ₹5 lakh for families of those who died; ₹1,500 per damaged coconut/oil palm tree; crop loss paid to bank accounts after field enumeration.

7 people died in Andhra Pradesh (CM, Oct 29). Odisha: at least 4 dead (3 of one family in a landslide at Raikia, Kandhamal; 1 in Gajapati). 12 missing after a landslide at Gidipabali, Ganjam; search on (SRC, Oct 31).
Odisha: floods now only in Ganjam. Rushikulya below danger mark; Jalaka (Balasore) has receded (SRC, Oct 31). Road links back in almost all Ganjam villages; one still cut off, relief by air.
Lightning warnings keep coming in AP and east Telangana. Stay indoors during thunderstorms; avoid trees, poles and open fields.

updates.x: Odisha landslides: 12 people are missing after a landslide hit hilltop Gidipabali village (Bhanjanagar block, Ganjam); about 25 people were there. One woman has been found. 160–170 Fire Services, SOG and NDRF personnel have been searching since last night. Odisha's toll is now at least 4: three of one family in a landslide at Raikia (Kandhamal) and one person in Gajapati. Floods remain only in Ganjam; the Rushikulya is below the danger mark and the Jalaka (Balasore) has receded. Ganjam: 1,05,622 people affected, 367 relief camps; Gajapati: 21,782 affected, 340 camps; cooked food going to all flood-hit villages. Also: IMD says the new Bay system should reach near the Andhra coast by Nov 2 evening.
updates.src: Odisha SRC via OmmCom News, Oct 31; IMD via Telangana Today, Oct 31

updates.x: Cyclone Arnab compensation, in one place. Crop rates per acre (AP, announced Oct 29): paddy ₹20,000; cotton, sugarcane, wheat ₹25,000; vegetables, tomato, papaya, pineapple ₹25,000; banana, turmeric, mango, cashew, coffee, dragon fruit ₹35,000; betel leaf ₹75,000; maize, ragi, bajra, black/green/Bengal gram, soybean, sunflower ₹15,000; coconut and oil palm ₹1,500 per tree. Also: ₹10,000 for a partly damaged house, ₹25,000 for a damaged shop, ₹3,000 for a two-wheeler, ₹10,000 for a three-wheeler, ₹1,000 per person who stayed in a relief camp, ₹5 lakh to families of those who died. Officials will assess damage village by village: keep photos of your loss and make sure your name is on the list. AP lightning alerts are still going out this afternoon.
updates.src: RTV English (AP govt), Oct 29; Deccan Chronicle, Oct 30; NDMA SACHET, Oct 31

updates.x: Rivers easing slowly. Ganjam: the Rushikulya at Purushottampur is down from 'severe' (Oct 30 evening) to 'above normal' flood (7 am today). Balasore: the Jalaka at Mathani Road Bridge is still in severe flood (6 am). Srikakulam: the Nagavali is above normal. Stay off flooded roads and causeways. Watch for the new Bay system: heavy rain in coastal AP & Yanam on Nov 1–3.
updates.src: NDMA SACHET (CWC, SRC Odisha), Oct 30–31; IMD via CareerIndia

updates.x: Lightning warning: the Andhra Pradesh government has been sending repeated thunderstorm alerts through the afternoon. During thunder and lightning, keep away from trees, towers, poles, fields and open ground, and stay inside a solid building. Balasore (Odisha): the Jalaka river is still in severe flood at Mathani Road Bridge.

Phone networks: 99.18% of mobile service is back in Andhra (West Godavari 98.5%, Konaseema 91.96%, the lowest). 11 Cell-on-Wheels towers sent in. If your own network is down, keep "Automatic network selection" on — you can roam onto another operator for free (intra-circle roaming is on). Odisha (Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal) improving as water recedes.

APSDMA: moderate rain today in Manyam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Konaseema, West Godavari, Prakasam, Nellore, Kadapa, Chittoor and Tirupati areas. IMD: heavy rain possible in Hyderabad, Rangareddy, Medchal, Yadadri, Nalgonda and Suryapet.

IMD's 9 am bulletin (Oct 31): the new system over the southeast Bay is expected to become a depression and move towards the Andhra coast by Nov 2. Isolated very heavy rain in coastal AP & Yanam on Nov 2–3. No cyclone or landfall point has been forecast so far. Arnab itself is over.

New weather system: IMD says a low over the South Andaman Sea is likely to become a depression over the southeast Bay around Oct 31 and move towards the Andhra Pradesh coast over the next two days. Isolated heavy to very heavy rain in coastal AP & Yanam on Nov 2–3; heavy rain in Telangana Nov 1–2 and Odisha Nov 2. Fishermen: do not go to sea off AP from Nov 1 to 4.
Odisha: yellow rain alert for Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Gajapati and Ganjam on Nov 1–2; orange (heavy to very heavy rain) for Malkangiri on Nov 2–3.
Odisha released an extra ₹20 crore to Ganjam for rescue, relief, medical help and road repair, after CM Majhi's aerial survey of Ganjam and Gajapati.

Odisha floods: 299 villages in 22 blocks of Ganjam and 711 villages in 7 blocks of Gajapati hit. 11,882 people moved to shelters in Ganjam and 17,441 in Gajapati. Food dropped by helicopter to cut-off villages; boats in use in Ganjam.

Phones and mobile data: AP telecom network availability is back to 99.18% (DoT). In Odisha, Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal networks are improving as floods recede. Emergency towers (COW) stay in place.
CWC: Rushikulya at Purushottampur (Ganjam, Odisha) has eased from severe to above-normal flood at 7 am. Still stay off the river banks.
CWC: Jalaka river at Mathani Road Bridge (Balasore, Odisha) still in severe flood at 6 am.

Howrah–Chennai main line restored: single line from Oct 29, 9:30 pm, second line Oct 30, 3:45 pm, between Ichchapuram and Jhadupudi. 40+ trains were cancelled, 40 diverted, 16 short-terminated and 30 rescheduled over two days.

mood.t: Relief across north Andhra as lights come back, but Konaseema villages still wait for poles to go up.
Kakinada at dawn: "Thank God, there was not as much damage this time." A 65-year-old at a shelter: "Our homes get flooded, and we have to stay in the water."
Rescued workers in Kakinada thanked police teams for reaching them in time.

faq.q: Is anyone missing in the Ganjam landslide (Cyclone Arnab)?
faq.a: Yes. On Oct 31 Odisha's Special Relief Commissioner said 12 people are missing after a landslide at hilltop Gidipabali village, Bhanjanagar block, Ganjam. One woman has been found. 160–170 Fire Services, SOG and NDRF personnel are searching. Odisha emergency: 112.

faq.q: My phone has no signal after Cyclone Arnab. What do I do?
faq.a: Mobile service is back for 99% of Andhra (Konaseema ~92%). Keep "Automatic network selection" on in phone settings, or pick any network manually — intra-circle roaming lets you use another operator when yours is down. Emergency 112 works on any network.

Yes. IMD says Arnab weakened into a well-marked low over Chhattisgarh on Oct 29 and kept weakening. There are no cyclone alerts now, only lightning/thunderstorm warnings and river floods in Ganjam and Balasore (Odisha).

faq.q: Is another cyclone coming to Andhra Pradesh after Arnab?
faq.a: IMD says a low over the Andaman Sea is likely to become a depression around Oct 31 and move towards the Andhra coast. It forecasts heavy to very heavy rain in coastal Andhra and Yanam on Nov 2–3 and heavy rain in Telangana on Nov 1–2. It has not been named a cyclone. Fishermen should not go to sea off AP from Nov 1 to 4. Spill will update when IMD does.

faq.q: Is Cyclone Arnab coming to Vizag or Hyderabad?
faq.a: No. The storm is over. Visakhapatnam's power is fully restored (APEPDCL, Oct 30). Hyderabad had no cyclone alert.

faq.q: Are trains cancelled due to Cyclone Arnab today?
faq.a: The Howrah–Chennai main line is fully open again since Oct 30, 3:45 pm, at reduced speed. Visakhapatnam–Kirandul Night Express (18515/18516) was cancelled till Nov 4. See the train list on this page or call 139.

faq.q: When will power come back in Konaseema?
faq.a: AP's Energy Minister set Saturday evening (Oct 31) as the target for full restoration. Konaseema lost about 8,000 poles, so it is the slowest. Across APEPDCL, 92% of affected villages had power by Oct 30. Call 1912 for your area.

faq.q: What compensation is given for Cyclone Arnab damage?
faq.a: Andhra Pradesh has announced: Crop rates per acre (AP, announced Oct 29): paddy ₹20,000; cotton, sugarcane, wheat ₹25,000; vegetables, tomato, papaya, pineapple ₹25,000; banana, turmeric, mango, cashew, coffee, dragon fruit ₹35,000; betel leaf ₹75,000; maize, ragi, bajra, black/green/Bengal gram, soybean, sunflower ₹15,000; coconut and oil palm ₹1,500 per tree. ₹10,000 for a partly damaged house; ₹25,000 for a damaged shop; ₹3,000 for a damaged two-wheeler and ₹10,000 for a three-wheeler; ₹1,000 per person who stayed in a relief camp; 25 kg rice plus 1 kg each of onions, sugar and potatoes for families whose homes flooded; ₹5 lakh to families of those who died. Money goes to bank accounts after the village-level damage survey.

faq.q: How do I claim crop loss for Cyclone Arnab?
faq.a: Officials are doing field-level enumeration now. Be present when they visit, keep your land and bank details ready, and make sure your crop loss is recorded. No separate online form has been announced.

faq.q: How many people died in Cyclone Arnab?
faq.a: Andhra Pradesh reported 7 deaths (CM, Oct 29). In Odisha, PTI reported 3 deaths in a landslide.

faq.q: Are schools open after Cyclone Arnab?
faq.a: AP closed schools Oct 27–28 in coastal districts. We have not seen any new closure order; check with your school.

faq.q: My family is in a cyclone-hit district. How do I check on them?
faq.a: Call the district control room on its page here. In AP you can also WhatsApp Mana Mitra on 9552300009 (send 'Hi').

safety: Stay indoors until officials say it's safe.
Keep away from the sea, rivers, canals and flooded roads.
Don't touch fallen lines or wet poles. Report on 1912 (AP).
Charge phones; keep a torch, water, medicines and documents in a plastic bag.
Never drive or walk through flood water.
Forward only what you can verify.

power.note: Oct 30: power back in 5,277 of 5,727 villages (92%), 535 of 552 substations, 22.2 lakh of 29.1 lakh homes/shops (76%) and 44,004 of 1.13 lakh farm connections. Fully restored: Visakhapatnam, Parvathipuram Manyam, Vizianagaram, Anakapalli, East Godavari, Kakinada, Eluru. Odisha: 13 of 20 lakh consumers were back by Oct 28 night. Target for full restoration: Oct 31 evening (Energy Minister). Never touch fallen wires; call 1912. Ganjam (Odisha): 80–85% of power network restored; Aska due back Oct 31 (SRC).

relief.summary: AP: 290 relief centres set up for 84,396 people; 3,100 pregnant women moved to hospitals (367 births). Odisha: 43,827 people moved to 634 shelters in 8 districts; no deaths.
relief.food: Families leaving AP relief camps get 25 kg rice, a packet of essentials and cash for immediate expenses. Fishermen and handloom workers are promised food aid. Food and water stay free at open relief centres; if not, call 1070. AP also gives 1 kg each of onions, sugar and potatoes to affected families, 25 kg rice where water entered homes, and ₹1,000 per person who stayed in a relief camp. Odisha: cooked food to all flood-hit villages in Ganjam and Gajapati (SRC, Oct 31).
